note: T5b-Y4 (the owner's decision of 2026-11-13; SPEC-multigraph-envelope.md section 3): the /search answer budget, mode plain: the rows alone (MATCHES). What a /search holds is priced while it is built, against --search-max-answer-memory-mb (4,096 MiB by default, staging's; 1 on the recording server so that the sample stays short; 0 = none): each pair's rows and their per-position values as they grow (a values account a pair), and the request's JSON answer, its text and the transport's and the cache's copies (one answer account a request). Past the bound the WHOLE request is refused 400, on a multi-graph server too (no pair is named, no envelope; whichever account passed), nothing partial sent, the work stopped where it passed: {error, code: "search_answer_too_large", max_memory_mb}, written in this order (error first, as the intake refusals and resolve_answer_too_large). The text is the same in every mode and on every route mode (abundance_sum, align); its advice: fewer top_labels, a larger discovery_fraction, fewer or shorter FASTA records, or no per-position values. A refused request is not cached: the same request is refused again. A request whose work fails for another reason after the budget passed is this refusal (the answer never depends on the order the pairs charged in). Below the bound every answer is the one without a budget, byte for byte. GET /capabilities states the bound (sample 12: multigraph.search; a single-graph server's top-level search). A real run: two copies of a pair whose 2,000 columns share one 100 bp stretch (the service's top_labels 10,000 case: each pair answers 2,000 rows), the request that stretch; at the default bound the same request answered 200 (846,676 bytes of text, the answer account 4,665,424 B, the values account at most 66,272 B a pair).
